tweets.text:
Breakthroughs in semiconductor manufacturing increasingly depend on infrastructure that powers fab operations, enabling advanced processes, improving efficiency, and supporting sustainability goals.  

In our latest blog, SEMI’s Mayura Padmanabhan spoke with Ilya Zabelinsky, founder of the International SubFab Research Labs (ISRL), to discuss the role of the subfab and why it is critical to the future of semiconductor manufacturing. 

“Throughout my career, I saw significant investments made in new transistor architectures, process technologies, materials, and manufacturing equipment,” Zabelinsky explained. “However, comparatively little effort was dedicated to understanding what happens to materials after they leave the process chamber or how those materials should be handled, treated, recycled, or neutralized.” 

Zabelinsky noted that industry-wide standards for helium leak detection is one area that could enable a common technical language across the semiconductor ecosystem, improving collaboration. 

Read the Q&A: https://www.semi.org/en/blogs/the-role-of-subfab-infrastructure-in-the-future-of-semiconductor-manufacturing?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_content=subfab%20q%26a%20blog

The headlines are dominated by the unprecedented growth in data centers and their rising energy consumption, along with the skyrocketing cost of AI inference. Perhaps less obvious is the direct connection between the two – reducing energy consumption reduces AI cost. 

Energy efficiency must be a strategic priority for all companies using AI inference, not just for data center builders. 

Did you know?:  

✅ AI training compute is growing an estimated 4-5x annually, with the largest models using trillions of parameters.

✅ Global data center electricity consumption is projected to double by 2030, straining global energy and water resources.

✅ AI infrastructure investments are expected to increase TENFOLD this year from just 5 years ago.

✅ Daily AI token consumption in the U.S. is projected to grow TENFOLD by 2030.

Dr. Pushkar Apte, Global Lead for Smart Data-AI Initiative at SEMI, breaks down how companies interested in AI computing can turn energy challenges into opportunities in our latest blog: 

Read the full blog: https://www.semi.org/en/blogs/three-strategic-imperatives-for-energy-efficient-ai-computing?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_content=energy%20efficiency%20blog

Today, SEMI and @SemiconIndia announced that Hon'ble Prime Minister @narendramodi will inaugurate SEMICON India 2026.   

India's semiconductor ambitions are entering a decisive new phase, fueled by landmark investments under the Ministry of Electronics & Information Technology (MeitY) Semicon India Programme.  

In this time of transformation, SEMI will host SEMICON India 2026 alongside ISM, MeitY, and the Government of India on September 17-19 under the theme, "Transform Tomorrow: Silicon to Systems – Building the Ecosystem." 

"SEMI has empowered the rise of semiconductor hubs around the world for more than five decades, and India is well positioned to thrive with its blend of speed, ambition, talent and long-term vision,” said Ajit Manocha, President of SEMI. “Through SEMICON India 2026, SEMI brings the collective strength of its global network to India’s journey. India’s opportunity is not simply to join the global supply chain, but to become integral to it. That is the ambition SEMICON India 2026 exists to accelerate." 

Learn more: https://www.semi.org/en/semi-press-release/honble-pm-shri-narendra-modi-to-inaugurate-semicon-india-2026-on-17th-september?utm_source=x&utm_medium=pr&utm_content=semicon%20india

AI, HBM and advanced logic are driving a stronger wafer fab materials outlook.

The latest SEMI-Linx Wafer Fab Materials Quarterly (WFMQ) 2Q 2026 shows wafer fab materials demand continuing to strengthen as semiconductor growth becomes increasingly shaped by advanced logic, memory and AI-related investment.

As device architectures become more complex, materials demand is being supported not only by market recovery, but also by rising process intensity across leading-edge applications. Photoresist, deposition materials, CMP, specialty gases and wet chemicals are among the segments benefiting from this trend.

The key takeaway: wafer fab materials growth is increasingly driven by technology mix, process complexity and materials intensity per wafer.

Learn more in the latest SEMI-Linx WFMQ 2Q 2026: https://www.semi.org/en/products-services/market-data/wafer-fab-materials-quarterly

A key takeaway from our recent AI Techniques in Semiconductor Manufacturing workshop: industrial AI success is less about the biggest model and more about the right foundation—domain expertise, high-quality context, knowledge graphs, and agentic workflows.

Physics-informed AI is gaining momentum for process optimization, predictive maintenance, and troubleshooting. But scalable adoption will depend on explainability, governance, and trust.

Thank you to our speakers and attendees for two days of thoughtful discussions and meaningful connections.

Learn more about Smart Manufacturing: https://www.semi.org/en/industry-groups/smart-manufacturing?utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_content=smart%20manufacturing%20group

Join us at the Smart Manufacturing Pavilion at SEMICON West 2026, October 13-15 at Moscone Center in San Francisco.

As global demand for semiconductors continues to rise, policies that strengthen domestic manufacturing are essential for long-term competitiveness. We commend the August 5 statement from Senate Finance Committee Chairman @MikeCrapo and Ranking Member @RonWyden, reaffirming support for the Section 48D Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit (AMIC). This follows SEMI's recent Tax Day event, where senior tax executives from our member companies visited Capitol Hill to discuss the importance of AMIC to the semiconductor supply chain.
 
“The joint statement from senators Crapo and Wyden in support of the Section 48D tax credit highlights the crucial role it plays in strengthening U.S. semiconductor manufacturing, creating jobs, and advancing national security,” said SEMI President and CEO Ajit Manocha. “Last month we shared on Capitol Hill how the looming AMIC expiration adds uncertainty for our member companies in the semiconductor supply chain, some of whom are actively planning to expand operations to meet rising chip demand, and we applaud the senators’ leadership for this pivotal tool in attracting semiconductor ecosystem investment.”
 
Learn more: https://www.semi.org/en/semi-press-release/semi-applauds-statement-from-senators-crapo-and-wyden-supporting-us-tax-credit-for-semiconductor-manufacturing?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=pr&utm_content=senate%20support%20us%20tax%20credit%20for%20semiconductor%20manufacturing
